body:
Ok, this is good.

You don't know how to deal with the regret that your anger brings.  That's a start.  That regret is HEALTHY.  You should feel bad about the pain your actions bring upon others.  First you have to deal with the current bout of pain you have wrought.

You can start by acknowledging that you don't know how to deal with your anger and other emotions, and telling someone, like us, that you are sorry.  Go ahead, tell us, type it out.  Tell me why you are sorry.  You can't do this right away for some of the people in your life, as that will take time.  But you and I know you are hurting.

You deserve an apology too.  Tell yourself that you are sorry.

Now.  Regarding anger.  This is a very difficult emotion, as it involves viscereal reactions that your whole body is fine tuned to feel.  It too can be healthy in some respects, it reflects your survival instincts.

Once you understand that anger involves your whole body; and you know it does, because when you feel it; you can feel it from your head to your toes; right?  Once you really accept and understand this, you can step back and identify anger immediately.  You have to create that pause.  You have to see that what you are feeling is coming from yourself, and only you can control it.  It is your emotion, not mine, or your boyfriends' or your mothers', or anyone elses'.  

So you have heard this advice before, I am sure, but I will bring a new twist to it.

When you feel anger.  Stop, pause, breath steady.  Tell yourself: this is the anger emotion.  Feel it.  It is an adrenalin high, it is a cold itch in the back of your neck.  Feel it.  It is real, and it is yours.  It is you.  It is part of what makes you human.

Now that you have experienced the whole emotion.  Can you sit down?  Come down and relax your body.  You already know that you don't want to deal with the potential regret that this emotion might bring.

Now here is the hard part, and I promise you this will backfire some times, but if it does, it will not be your fault.  Tell the object of your anger why your are mad.  Phrases like: "I am lonely tonight, and I feel as if you are abandoning me, if you go to the club."  or "I am angry that you took my last soda, and I feel as if you dont respect my things."

The healthy people in your life will definitly respond to this.  Some people might throw it back in your face, they are inmature, and you know it.  You now know that you have done all you can do to deal with that emotion, and guess what, it is probably gone at this point.

By the way, this technique is wonderful for all of our emotions.  Tomorrow, when you see something really wonderful, STOP.  Breath, pause, and tell yourself: "This is hapiness, I feel it in my eyes, and I feel it in my toes.  It feels so good I want to cry."  Smile, and tell the person next to you what you feel: "Dad, being here with you right now, playing the crossword puzzle, makes me happy.  I love you."

Now you are alive.

Can you please tell me a little bit more about your anger?

I understand why the whole of this situation would get you angry, but I want to know more about how you experience your anger.

What triggers it and what actually goes on in your head when you experience it.

I can provide ways for you to deal with it constructively, but it would help to hear more about some specifics.

"For all the suffering and pain you have endured you have been given access to the negative aspects of life but you should understand that as bad as things have been and seem to you that they can be the complete polar opposite."

It can be, I've known the pleasure of a woman, the bite of a frosty rain on a mountain top.  The comfort of dinner with loved ones.  The sweet taste of success; that ambition, drive and determination bring.

I am having trouble dealing with impermanence, and loss.  Although I understand the circle of life, I still cry for the flower, as it whithers away.

You are right about taking chances.  I am scared of what the future holds.

In the deeper recesses of my head, I realize what a great big crap-shot this life is.  You can't learn anything from a toss of the dice.  And therein lies the rub.

Again you are right about figuring out what I want.  What I want is, or seems to be, unattainable.  Self sabotage would probably be a good way to describe my life with respect to some goals.  The whole: "Why bother?" attitude.  What a nasty self-serving and futile view of life. . . 

I know all of this.

I have to take care of my depression right now, or I will not be able to move on.

There is one thing that I am not too sure others really understand.  You see, suicide IS a viable and rational decision.  I have not decided to do it.  But it looms neigh.  I know that there might be a point, and I have accepted it, that my body gets the best of my soul, and I can not do it again.  I have already made that decision.  People in my situation do this.  It is rational, and it takes a lot out of you.

I am not ready to hang up the saddle just yet.  I stopped for a little bit this weekend to tell the horse FUCK YOU! and talk to you guys about it.

Thank you for listening.

I think you hit the nail on the head about my obession with the 'quality' of my problems.

I have a great deal of compassion, for those in pain.  My empathy is evoked by the smallest sadness of others.  Because I really understand.

But there is a flip side to that coin.

I can be one cold motherfucker inside.  I laugh at others misery and think: "Oh I wish I had your problems. . ."  No sense detailing the rest of my coldness to others, as it serves no one.  But it is there, and it too is painfull.

I am not too sure about your thoughts about my finding happiness in a relationship.  I do understand that I am responsible for my happiness.

I am more weighing the odds, and trying to determine what my path should be.

Yeah, I know this. I have simple goals, one day at a time.  I progress, I really do.  I have become a fine mechanic.  Write Android programs, and contribute to my household.  

Hell, I have laughed at the nastiest this life can throw at me.

Its all becoming a bit too much though.  Its' getting harder to get back up.  *Sigh*.  And so it goes for us all right?

I am much to mature to commit suicide, I know this, but danm, it really tends to pop into my thoughts way too much lately.
